description: We are a team of enthusiastic students passionate about space science, technology, research, and innovation. We aim to use NASA’s open data to explore real-world challenges and develop creative, meaningful solutions. By combining our skills in research, design, presentation, and technology, we hope to create an engaging project while learning and collaborating as a team.
summary: Echoes Beyond Earth is a visual storytelling project that explores NASA's discarded and abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars. It presents the stories behind these objects, explaining why they were used, how they contributed to space exploration, and why they were left behind. Through mission timelines, artifact story cards, and an interactive space museum concept, the project makes space exploration history easier and more interesting to understand. It highlights missions such as Apollo, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and InSight. Our goal is to show that even after a mission ends, the equipment left behind continues to represent human curiosity, scientific discoveries, and the legacy of space exploration.
details: Echoes Beyond Earth is a visual storytelling project that explores NASA's equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Our project presents the history and importance of these objects through a structured presentation, mission timelines, and artifact story cards. It covers Apollo missions and Mars exploration missions such as Pathfinder, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and InSight. Each artifact is explained through six questions: Where was it used? What was it? Why was it needed? How did it work? Why was it left behind? What is its legacy? We collected information from NASA and NASA/JPL resources and transformed technical mission information into simple, engaging stories that students and the general public can understand. Our proposed future development is an interactive digital space museum where users can explore mission timelines, discover individual artifacts, and learn about their contributions to space science. The main objective is to show that equipment left behind is not meaningless waste but a lasting record of human exploration, scientific discoveries, and technological progress.
